ordinary_frame.basis: This source appoints a First Lesson and Gradual followed by a Second Lesson and the Tract before the Gospel. The generic Ordinary frame has no repeated-reading module. A specialized frame has not yet been modeled, so the generic frame is withheld without treating any of these source rows as absent.

provenance.provenance_evidence: The project-owned projection passage reproduces the retained calendar body hash exactly. Its artifact manifest records the bounded public-domain 1862 Pustet antecedent, the separate 1962 target, and every editorial transformation; neither witness is represented as owning the projected bytes. The 1962 reading was established on that edition's page images rather than its text layer, cross-read against the Benziger conformed printing. Differences from the antecedent: 1862 text layer damages 4 place(s) in this prayer; at each the 1962 word and the layer's reading are: preces -> qreces; quesumus domine -> qusesumus l d mine; aduersantia -> aduer santia; tue maiestatis extende -> tuse maiestd tis ext nde per d minum; 1922 Mame text layer damages 3 place(s) here (chiefly its OCR of the ae/oe ligatures and of the acute accents): preces -> eces; quesumus -> queesu panis; tue -> tuze; both antecedents print the ae and oe ligatures and the printed acute accents, and use the j-orthography; this transcription follows the repository convention recorded in src/sources/calendars/roman-1962/propers.yaml (j retained, ae/oe digraphs written as two letters, no accent marks). Corroboration: 1922 Mame, editio quarta iuxta typicam Vaticanam (public domain), printed p. 87, artifact PDF p. 201; Benziger 1962 conformed printing OCR at djvu text line 27401 (comparison witness only, rights_status unresolved; never a publication basis); the 1604 and 1570 were not consulted for this oration - the 1862 and the 1922 Mame between them read the whole prayer.

propers.text:
Preces nostras, quaesumus, Domine, clementer exaudi: et contra cuncta nobis
adversantia, dexteram tuae majestatis extende. Per Dominum.
